alert.name: ConsumerLagHigh
alert.summary: The ledger consumer group is 250 messages behind on the topic provider-events, all partitions together; the threshold is 50.

diagnosis.hypothesis: The alert is a transient startup backlog, not a fault. Every container was recreated at 01:33:00, about 5 minutes before the alert. The ledger consumer group had to catch up on provider-events, and the provider redelivered unacknowledged webhooks, which produced a burst of 250 messages of lag. The consumers have since drained it: lag is 0 on all partitions. The ledger consumer is posting events normally, and the redeliveries show up as already_processed, which the idempotent handler skips safely. I did not observe the 250-message peak itself, because the lag series only start at 01:33-01:34. That the restart caused the backlog is inferred from timing, not shown directly.

evidence.shows: Summed consumer lag is 0 from 01:34:28 to 01:38:28, so the symptom is no longer present. Only one point at 01:33 shows a value (1.0).
Per-partition lag is 0 for the ledger and payment-confirmer groups on all 3 partitions at 01:34, 01:36 and 01:38. The series begin only at 01:34, so the 250 peak was not seen.

The ledger consumer's posted rate climbs from 0.24/s to 3.5/s after 01:33 and its already_processed rate stays low. The payment-confirmer also processes normally. This is the pattern of a consumer catching up after a restart.

All services, including ledger-consumer, were recreated at 01:33:00 with the same image and idempotent/dead_letter settings. No single-service change stands out, and the restart of the whole stack matches the timing of the backlog.

The money check passed all five invariants: 1133 provider events were each posted exactly once, the ledger is balanced, and the ledger, payments and refunds all match the provider's records. No money was affected.
ledger-consumer logged no ERROR lines in the last 30 minutes, so there is no sign of a failing handler or poison messages.

proposed_fix.summary: No fix needed: the lag has cleared by itself and the books are correct. Optionally, tune the alert to ignore the first few minutes after a planned restart, or require lag above 50 for several minutes, so a restart catch-up does not page. If lag comes back without a restart, investigate then.

diagnosis.blast_radius: No action is proposed, so nothing is affected. An alert-rule change would only alter when this alert pages.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Not applicable, as no system change is made. Revert any alert-rule tweak by restoring the previous threshold and duration.
